record.title: The BCH weight-enumerator integrality conjecture
record.statement:
Let $m$ and $t$ be integers, and let $C$ be obtained by adding an overall parity check to the primitive BCH code of length $2^m-1$ and designed distance $2t-1$. Thus $C$ has length $n=2^m$ and minimal distance $d\ge 2t$. Let $d'$ be the smallest power of $2$ satisfying $d'\ge 2t$, and let $\mathcal{P}_s$ denote the class of generating functions whose $s$th roots have integral coefficients. **The BCH weight-enumerator integrality conjecture.** The weight enumerator of $C$ belongs to

$$
\mathcal{P}_{2^m/d'}.
$$

This is presented as a conjectural analogue of the theorem for Reed–Muller codes; the source gives no proof or resolution.
record.source_name: Nadia Heninger, E. M. Rains and N. J. A. Sloane, “On the Integrality of n-th Roots of Generating Functions”, arXiv:math/0509316 (2006).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0509316

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2005).

record.title: Flatness and Koszulity conjecture for preprojective algebras of non-ADET graphs
record.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a connected graph with adjacency matrix $A$, and let $P({\bf \Gamma})$ be the associated preprojective algebra, constructed from a choice of field $k$ and a modulating space with nondegenerate pairing $E$. The **flatness and Koszulity conjecture.** (i) The family of preprojective algebras $P({\bf \Gamma})$ is flat: for every choice of $k$ and $E$, its matrix Hilbert series is constant. If $\Gamma$ is not of ADET type, this Hilbert series is

$$
(1-At+t^2)^{-1}.
$$

(ii) If $\Gamma$ is not of ADET type, then the algebras $P({\bf \Gamma})$ are Koszul.

The claim concerns deformation-invariance of the graded structure of these preprojective algebras and their homological properties outside the ADET cases. The source records no resolution or counterexample, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Victor Ostrik, “Module categories over representations of SL_q(2) in the non-semisimple case”, arXiv:math/0509530 (2006).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0509530

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2005).

record.title: The characterization of maximum complete and empty subgraphs in the quadrance graph
record.statement:
Let $F_q$ be the finite field with $q$ elements, and let $V_q$ be the graph on $F_q\times F_q$ whose adjacency is determined by the quadrance relation used in the paper. For a subset $U\subseteq V_q$, say that $U$ spans a **complete subgraph** or an **empty subgraph** according as every pair of vertices in $U$ is adjacent or no pair is adjacent.

**Maximum subgraph conjecture.** If $U$ spans a complete subgraph or an empty subgraph of order $q$ in $V_q$, then $U$ is a line in $F_q\times F_q$.

The preceding bound shows that a complete or empty subgraph of this type has at most $q$ vertices, and equality is attained by the $q$ points on a line. Computations for $q=3$ and $q=7$ support the conjectured converse.
record.source_name: Le Anh Vinh, “Quadrance polygons, association schemes and strongly regular graphs”, arXiv:math/0509598 (2005).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0509598

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2005).

record.title: Hamiltonian cycle game's threshold conjecture
record.statement:
Let ${\cal H}$ be the set of Hamiltonian cycles in $K_n$. For a family of winning sets ${\cal F}$, let $b_{\cal F}^p$ denote the smallest bias for which Breaker wins the random game on the edges of $G(n,p)$, and let $p_{\cal F}$ denote the threshold probability for Maker's win. **Hamiltonian cycle game's threshold conjecture.** There exists a constant $C$ such that

$$
b_{{\cal H}}^p = \Theta\left(p\frac{n}{\log n}\right), \qquad p\geq C\frac{\log n}{n}.
$$

In particular, $p_{{\cal H}}=\frac{\log n}{n}$. This conjecture asserts that the Hamiltonian cycle game has the same threshold behaviour as the connectivity and perfect matching games; the paper establishes corresponding results for several other games but leaves this Hamiltonian-cycle assertion open.
record.source_name: Milos Stojakovic and Tibor Szabo, “Positional games on random graphs”, arXiv:math/0601659 (2006).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0601659

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2006).

record.title: Mills–Robbins–Rumsey's monotone-triangle correspondence conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\TSPP{n}^{k}$ be the subset of triangular shifted plane partitions whose entries in the first $n-1-k$ columns attain their maximal values $n$. Let $\MT{n}^{k}$ be the set of monotone triangles whose entries in the first $n-k$ columns attain their minimum values $j-i+1$. **Mills–Robbins–Rumsey's monotone-triangle correspondence conjecture.** For $n\geq2$ and $k=0,1,\dots,n-1$,

$$
\lvert\TSPP{n}^{k}\rvert=\lvert\MT{n}^{k}\rvert.
$$

This proposes an equality between restricted TSSCPPs and restricted monotone triangles, extending the known correspondence between alternating sign matrices and monotone triangles.
record.source_name: Masao Ishikawa, “On refined enumerations of totally symmetric self-complementary plane partitions I”, arXiv:math/0602068 (2006).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0602068

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2006). “This number is famous for the alternating sign matrix conjecture (cf. ). The number of totally symmetric self-complementary plane partitions was conjectured to be $A_n$ in , and settled in and (see al”

record.title: Parity edge-coloring numbers of balanced complete bipartite graphs
record.statement:
Let $K_{n,n}$ be the complete bipartite graph with $n$ vertices in each part. Let $p(G)$ and $\widehat{p}(G)$ denote the minimum numbers of colors in a parity edge-coloring and a strong parity edge-coloring, respectively. **The balanced complete-bipartite parity edge-coloring conjecture.**

$$
p(K_{n,n})=\widehat{p}(K_{n,n})=2^{\lfloor\lg n\rfloor}.
$$

The paper states that the value of $\widehat{p}(K_{n,n})$ is known for $n\le8$, while the general case remains open.
record.source_name: David P. Bunde, Kevin Milans, Douglas B. West and Hehui Wu, “Parity Edge-Coloring of Graphs”, arXiv:math/0602341 (2006).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0602341

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2006).

record.title: Conger's Steiner-point degree conjecture for elliptic Minkowski spaces
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{M}^n$ be a piece-wise differentiable, elliptic Minkowski space, and let $s(\mathbb{M}^n)$ denote the maximum degree of a Steiner point in a Steiner minimal tree in $\mathbb{M}^n$. **Conger's conjecture.** For any such $\mathbb{M}^n$,

$$
s(\mathbb{M}^n)\leq 2n.
$$

The paper gives results for the norms $\lVert\cdot\rVert_1+\lambda\lVert\cdot\rVert_2$ that support the bound in several parameter ranges, while leaving the conjecture open for general piece-wise differentiable, elliptic Minkowski spaces.
record.source_name: Konrad J Swanepoel, “The local Steiner problem in finite-dimensional normed spaces”, arXiv:math/0603616 (2006).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0603616

record.title: Connectivity bound for graphs exceeding Reed's bound
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, with chromatic number $\chi$, clique number $\omega$, maximum degree $\Delta$, order $n$, and let $\overline{\kappa}=\kappa(\overline{G})$ denote the connectivity of its complement. The **connectivity bound conjecture.** There exists a constant $C>0$ such that

$$
\chi>\left\lceil\frac{1}{2}(\omega+\Delta+1)\right\rceil\Rightarrow\overline{\kappa}\geq C\log(n).
$$

This is intended to express that a graph violating Reed's conjectural upper bound must have a highly connected complement; the supplied source gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: landon rabern, “New upper bounds on the chromatic number of a graph”, arXiv:math/0606632 (2006).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0606632

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2006).

record.title: Conjecture on diagonal-flip stabilization of surface triangulations
record.statement:
For a surface $S$, let $N(S)$ be the minimum value such that any two triangulations $T$ and $T'$ of $S$ with

$$
|V(T)|=|V(T')|\geq N(S)
$$

are equivalent under diagonal flips. Let $V_{\min}(S)$ be the minimum number of vertices in a triangulation of $S$.

**Conjecture on diagonal-flip stabilization.** The only surfaces $S$ for which

$$
N(S)=V_{\min}(S)
$$

are $S_0$, $S_1$, $S_2$, $N_1$, $N_2$, and $N_3$.

The equality means that flip-equivalence already holds at the minimum triangulation size. It is verified for the listed surfaces, while the paper gives counterexamples showing strict inequality for many higher-genus surfaces; the full exclusivity claim is left as a conjecture.
record.source_name: Thom Sulanke, “Irreducible triangulations of low genus surfaces”, arXiv:math/0606690 (2006).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0606690

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2006).

record.title: Finite-plane Besicovitch set cardinality conjecture
record.statement:
For an odd prime power $q$, a **Besicovitch set** in ${\mathbb{F}_q}^2$ is a subset containing a line in every direction. **Finite-plane Besicovitch set conjecture.** The smallest Besicovitch set in ${\mathbb{F}_q}^2$ has cardinality

$$
\frac{q(q+1)}{2}+\frac{q-1}{2}.
$$

Every such set has cardinality at least $q^2/2$, while the source describes a construction attaining the displayed upper bound. The conjecture gives the exact minimum in the finite plane for odd prime powers.
record.source_name: Joshua N. Cooper, “Collinear Triple Hypergraphs and the Finite Plane Kakeya Problem”, arXiv:math/0607734 (2006).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0607734

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2006).

record.title: Spectral Turán conjecture for the two largest adjacency eigenvalues
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with $m$ edges that contains no complete subgraph $K_{r+1}$. Write $\mu_1(G)\geq \mu_2(G)\geq\cdots$ for the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix. **Spectral Turán conjecture.** One should have

$$
\mu_1^2(G)+\mu_2^2(G)\leq\frac{r-1}{r}2m.
$$

This is proposed as a spectral generalization of Turán's theorem, extending the known bound involving only the largest adjacency eigenvalue. Its status is not established in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Bela Bollobas and Vladimir Nikiforov, “Cliques and the Spectral Radius”, arXiv:math/0608453 (2006).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0608453

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2006).

record.title: The maximal-imaginary-part conjecture for roots of SNN polynomials
record.statement: Let $M_d(t)$ be the polynomial associated with degree $d$, and let $\gamma_d$ be a root of $M_d(t)$ with largest norm. An **SNN polynomial** is a degree-$d$ polynomial satisfying Stanley's non-negativity condition. **Maximal-imaginary-part conjecture.** The quantity $|\operatorname{Im}(\gamma_d)|$ is maximal among the imaginary parts of all roots of degree-$d$ SNN polynomials. Experimental data for SNN polynomials of degree at most seven support this conjecture; it is proved in the source when $d=2$.
record.source_name: Benjamin Braun and Mike Develin, “Ehrhart Polynomial Roots and Stanley's Non-negativity Theorem”, arXiv:math/0610399 (2006).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0610399

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2006).

record.title: The minimal book embedding conjecture for graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $mnl(G)$ denote the minimum number of links among spatial embeddings of $G$. A **book embedding** is a spatial embedding in which the graph is embedded with respect to a book structure, and a minimal book embedding is one having the minimum number of links among book embeddings of $G$. **Minimal book embedding conjecture.** For any graph $G$, there is a minimal book embedding of $G$ which realizes

$$
mnl(G).
$$

The conjecture is suggested by computations for canonical book representations of complete graphs, including the example for $K_8$. It asserts that the global minimum number of links is always attained by a book embedding; the general claim remains open.
record.source_name: Tom Fleming and Blake Mellor, “Counting Links in Complete Graphs”, arXiv:math/0611626 (2006).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0611626

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2006).

record.title: The prime pure alternance graph conjecture
record.statement: A bicoloured alternance graph is called **pure** and **prime** in the sense developed in the paper; connectedness is with respect to the underlying graph. The white one-point graph and the white pentagon determine the specified parity class. **Prime pure alternance graph conjecture.** The only connected prime pure alternance graphs are the white one-point graph and the graphs in the parity class of the white pentagon. The source says this conjecture is equivalent to the preceding edge-cut conjecture and that, together, they would imply the Cycle Double Cover Conjecture; no resolution is supplied.
record.source_name: François Genest, “Eulerian graphs and local complementation”, arXiv:math/0701421 (2007).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0701421

record.title: The almost-uniform extremal conjecture for Sperner partition systems
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{P}^n_k$ be the family of $k$-partitions of an $n$-set, and call a partition system **Sperner** when the collection of all its classes is a Sperner set system. An almost-uniform partition has class sizes differing by at most one.

**Almost-uniform extremal conjecture.** For positive integers $n,k$, a largest Sperner partition system in $\mathcal{P}^n_k$ is an almost-uniform partition system.

The paper proves an upper bound using the LYM inequality but leaves the exact cardinality and structure of extremal systems open.
record.source_name: Karen Meagher, “Covering arrays on graphs: qualitative independence graphs and extremal set partition theory”, arXiv:math/0701553 (2007).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0701553

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2007).

record.title: Erdős et al.'s conjecture on avoiding triangles in two-colored planes
record.statement: Let $T$ be a triangle in the Euclidean plane, and let a **coloring** be a partition of $\mathbb{R}^2$ into two color classes. A coloring **contains** $T$ if it has a monochromatic copy of $T$ obtained by translations and rotations; otherwise, it **avoids** $T$. Let $\chi^*$ be the coloring by alternating half-open horizontal strips of width $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, with a point $(x,y)$ black if and only if $n\sqrt{3}<y\leq\left(n+\frac{1}{2}\right)\sqrt{3}$ for some integer $n$. **Erdős et al.'s conjecture.** For every triangle $T$ and every coloring $\chi$, if $\chi$ avoids $T$, then $T$ is an equilateral $(l,l,l)$-triangle and $\chi$ is equal to an $l$-times scaled copy of $\chi^*$, up to possible modifications of the colors of points on the boundary of the strips. The paper presents a counterexample to this conjecture and gives a broader class of colorings avoiding the unit triangle, so this conjecture is refuted.
record.source_name: Vit Jelinek, Jan Kyncl, Rudolf Stolar and Tomas Valla, “Monochromatic triangles in two-colored plane”, arXiv:math/0701940 (2007).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0701940

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2007).

record.title: Recursive structure conjecture for extremal polyominoes
record.statement: Let $P$ be a $d$-dimensional polyomino with parameters $l_1,\dots,l_d$ and $v_1,\dots,v_d$, and suppose that the convex hull of $P$ has maximum volume. Let $P'$ be a subpolyomino of $P$. **Recursive structure conjecture.** The parameters satisfy $v_1=\dots=v_d=0$, and $P'$ can be chosen so that: (i) $P'$ has height $1$ in the direction of axis $i$; (ii) the projection of $P'$ along axis $i$ also has maximal convex-hull volume and parameters $l_1,\dots,l_{i-1},l_{i+1},\dots,l_d$; and (iii) $P$ can be decomposed into $P'$ and at most two orthogonal linear arms. This describes a recursive structure for maximizers, although the surrounding proof of the main theorem suggests that the assertion may already follow from established arguments in the paper.
record.source_name: Sascha Kurz, “Convex hulls of polyominoes”, arXiv:math/0702786 (2007).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0702786

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2007).

record.title: Albertson–Grossman–Haas partial list coloring conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph with list-chromatic number $\chi_{\ell}$. For a positive integer $t\leq\chi_{\ell}$, assign each vertex a list of $t$ colors, and let $\lambda_t$ be the minimum, over all such list assignments, of the maximum number of vertices that can be properly colored from their lists. **Albertson–Grossman–Haas conjecture.** If $t\leq\chi_{\ell}$, then

$$
\lambda_t\geq\frac{tn}{\chi_{\ell}}.
$$

Equivalently, at least $tn/\chi_{\ell}$ vertices can be colored from every assignment of lists of size $t$. The conjecture is known in the cases $t=1$ and $t=\chi_{\ell}$, but remains open for $1<t<\chi_{\ell}$.
record.source_name: Glenn G. Chappell, “A Lower Bound for Partial List Colorings”, arXiv:math/9805066 (1998).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9805066

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 1998). “However, the conjecture remains open for $1<t<\chl$.”

record.title: Chan–Robbins–Yuen volume conjecture for the polytope of restricted permutation matrices
record.statement:
Let $n\ge 2$ and let $T_n$ be the set of $n\times n$ permutation matrices $\pi$ satisfying $\pi_{ij}=0$ for $j\ge i+2$. Let $P_n$ be the convex hull of $T_n$, and let $V_n$ denote its relative volume, measured in units of the minimum-volume simplex with vertices in the affine lattice spanned by $T_n$.

**Chan–Robbins–Yuen volume conjecture.** The relative volume of $P_n$ is

$$
V_n=\prod_{i=0}^{n-2}\frac{1}{i+1}\binom{2i}{i},
$$

the product of the first $n-1$ Catalan numbers.

The conjecture gives an explicit Catalan-product formula for the volume of this polytope; the paper presents it as the main claim for which evidence is provided, but does not establish the formula.
record.source_name: Clara S. Chan, David P. Robbins and David S. Yuen, “On the volume of a certain polytope”, arXiv:math/9810154 (1998).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9810154

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 1998).

record.title: The maximum-spanning-tree conjecture for Moore graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph, and let $\tau(G)$ denote its number of spanning trees. A $k$-regular graph of girth $g$ with the minimum possible number of vertices is called a $(k,g)$-cage; when it attains the Moore bound, it is a **Moore graph**. **Moore-graph spanning-tree conjecture.** Moore graphs have the maximum number of spanning trees among all simple graphs with the same number of vertices and edges.

This conjecture extends the observed extremal behavior of complete graphs, complete bipartite graphs, and the Petersen graph, but the source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Dmitry Jakobson and Igor Rivin, “On some extremal problems in graph theory”, arXiv:math/9907050 (1999).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9907050

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 1999).

record.title: The Clifford bound conjecture for unitary 2-designs
record.statement:
Let $d$ be the dimension of the underlying Hilbert space, and let a **unitary 2-design** be a set of unitary matrices whose second moments reproduce those of the Haar measure. The Clifford bound is

$$
d^4-d^2.
$$

**Clifford bound conjecture.** The cardinality of any unitary 2-design is at least

$$
d^4-d^2.
$$

The bound is attained by Clifford 2-designs in several dimensions and is known to be the smallest possible cardinality for designs based on the Clifford group. The conjecture asserts that no unitary 2-design, including one not based on the Clifford group, can be smaller.
record.source_name: D. Gross, K. Audenaert and J. Eisert, “Evenly distributed unitaries: on the structure of unitary designs”, arXiv:quant-ph/0611002 (2007).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0611002

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2006).

record.title: MED decomposition conjecture for subcubic 2-connected graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a 2-connected graph with maximum degree 3. A **MED decomposition** of $G$ is a decomposition of its edges into a matching, a union of disjoint even cycles, and an independent set of double-stars.

**MED decomposition conjecture.** Every 2-connected graph with maximum degree 3 has a MED decomposition.

MED decompositions are used to establish $(7,2)$-edge-choosability for several classes of cubic graphs, including many snarks. The source does not give a resolution of this conjecture.
record.source_name: Daniel W. Cranston and Douglas B. West, “Classes of 3-regular graphs that are (7, 2)-edge-choosable”, arXiv:0806.1348 (2008).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0806.1348

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2008).

record.title: Monotonicity and uniqueness conjecture for the smallest eigenvalue
record.statement: Let $\Lambda_\kappa$ denote the smallest eigenvalue of the relevant weighted spherical operator, with parameter $\kappa>0$ in dimension $n$. Proposition~ gives three possible alternatives for the eigenspace associated with $\Lambda_\kappa$. **Monotonicity and uniqueness conjecture.** (i) When $\kappa>0$ and $n\geqslant3$, only statement (ii) of Proposition~ is true. (ii) The function $\kappa\mapsto\Lambda_\kappa$ is increasing. This conjecture refines the proposition and is based on numerical experiments; its validity is not established in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Pierre Degond, Amic Frouvelle and Jian-Guo Liu, “Macroscopic limits and phase transition in a system of self-propelled particles”, arXiv:1109.2404 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1109.2404

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2011).

record.title: Optimality of the Theorem uj1 algorithm for one defective search
record.statement:
Let $g(n,k,\alpha,m)$ denote the minimum number of group-testing queries in the model considered, and let $a$ be the query-size parameter. Assume that $\frac{1}{\alpha}$ is an integer and

$$
k+\log k+1\leq \left\lceil \frac{n}{a}\right\rceil.
$$

**Optimality conjecture.** Under these assumptions, the algorithm used in the proof of Theorem uj1 is optimal for $m=1$. The preceding discussion indicates that the algorithm seems optimal under the stated condition, while noting counterexamples when $1/\alpha$ is not an integer; the exact values of $g(n,k,\alpha,m)$ are otherwise difficult to determine.
record.source_name: Dániel Gerbner, Balázs Keszegh, Dömötör Pálvölgyi and Gábor Wiener, “Density-based group testing”, arXiv:1204.1464 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1204.1464

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2012).

record.title: Ilić–Stevanović's spectral-moment conjecture for Volkmann trees
record.statement:
Let $n$ and $\Delta$ be positive integers, and let $k\geq 2$. Consider the Volkmann tree on $n$ vertices with maximum degree $\Delta$, as defined in the source.

**Ilić–Stevanović's conjecture.** The Volkmann tree has maximum spectral moment

$$
\operatorname{M}_{2k}
$$

among all trees on $n$ vertices with maximum degree $\Delta$.

The conjecture is a corollary of the paper's theorems on greedy trees and spectral moments for fixed degree sequences; the source does not provide an independent resolution status.
record.source_name: Eric Ould Dadah Andriantiana and Stephan Wagner, “Spectral moments of trees with given degree sequence”, arXiv:1304.4696 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.4696

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of April 2013); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: The semi-arc k-visibility graph edge-maximization conjecture
record.statement:
A **semi-arc $k$-visibility graph** is a graph represented by semi-arcs, with visibility allowing at most $k$ obstructing semi-arcs; let $n$ be the number of vertices. **Semi-arc $k$-visibility graph edge-maximization conjecture.** The maximum number of edges in a semi-arc $k$-visibility graph on $n$ vertices is

$$
(k+1)\left(2n-\frac{3k+6}{2}\right)
$$

for $n \geq 3k+3$. This conjecture would determine the extremal edge count beyond the open range identified in the paper; the stated bound is conjectured to be tight.
record.source_name: Matthew Babbitt, J. T. Geneson and Tanya Khovanova, “On k-visibility graphs”, arXiv:1305.0505 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.0505

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2013). “There are also similar open questions about arc $k$-visibility graphs.”

record.title: Polynomial-time computation of poset dimension from a linear extension graph
record.statement:
Let $P$ be a poset and let $G_L(P)$ be its linear extension graph, whose vertices are the linear extensions of $P$. The **dimension** $\dim(P)$ is the minimum size of a realizer of $P$, that is, a set of linear extensions whose intersection is $P$.

**Polynomial-time dimension conjecture.** The dimension of a poset given its linear extension graph can be determined in polynomial time.

The proposition preceding this conjecture gives a quasi-polynomial-time algorithm, while the conjecture asks whether this can be improved to polynomial time. This would match the expected complexity suggested by the exponential size of a linear extension graph relative to the underlying poset.
record.source_name: Marie Albenque and Kolja Knauer, “Convexity in partial cubes: the hull number”, arXiv:1309.5724 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.5724

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2013).

record.title: Partition-dependence conjecture for divisor and orbit polynomial leading coefficients
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a $Z_n$ curve described by the family in the source. For each positive integer $c$, let $x_c$ be the number of indices $i$ with $c_i=c$, and for each positive integer $d$, let $y_d$ be the number of indices $i$ with $d_i=d$:

$$
x_c=\left|\{i\mid c_i=c\}\right|,\qquad y_d=\left|\{i\mid d_i=d\}\right|.
$$

Thus $p=\sum_c x_c$ and $q=\sum_d y_d$ determine partitions of $p$ and $q$, respectively. **Partition-dependence conjecture.** The leading coefficients of the two polynomials in the polynomial-growth conjecture depend only on these partitions of $p$ and $q$. This is a refinement of the preceding conjecture: the source reports it as a pattern suggested by the numerical examples, without proving the asserted dependence.
record.source_name: Shaul Zemel, “Thomae Formulae for General Fully Ramified Z_n Curves”, arXiv:1311.4717 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.4717

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2013).

record.title: Akbari et al.'s upper-bound conjecture for edge Roman domination
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph of maximum degree $\Delta$ on $n$ vertices. An **edge Roman dominating function** is a function $f\colon E(G)\to\{0,1,2\}$ such that every edge assigned $0$ is adjacent to an edge assigned $2$, and the **edge Roman domination number** $\gamma'_R(G)$ is the minimum weight $\sum_{e\in E(G)}f(e)$ of such a function.

**Akbari et al.'s conjecture.**

$$
\gamma'_R(G)\leq\left\lceil\frac{\Delta}{\Delta+1}n\right\rceil.
$$

This conjecture seeks an upper bound for edge Roman domination in terms of the order and maximum degree of the graph, rather than its number of edges. The supplied text gives the preceding weaker bound $\gamma'_R(G)\leq\frac{2\Delta}{2\Delta+1}n$ but provides no resolution of the conjecture.
record.source_name: Gerard J. Chang, Sheng-Hua Chen and Chun-Hung Liu, “Edge Roman domination on graphs”, arXiv:1405.5622 (2014).

record.title: The conjecture that the modified Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv constant of $Z_p^3$ equals $9p-8$
record.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, and let $s_1(Z_p^3)$ denote the least integer $\ell$ such that every sequence of length $\ell$ in the finite abelian group $Z_p^3$ contains a zero-sum subsequence of length $p$. **Conjecture.**

$$
s_1(Z_p^3)=9p-8.
$$

The conjecture gives the expected exact value of this zero-sum constant; the surrounding discussion notes that proving a lower bound or an upper bound of comparable size would be significant. Its status is not resolved in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Satwik Mukherjee, “Some Results on Zero Sum Sequences in Z_p^3”, arXiv:1409.2843 (2014).

record.title: Polynomial-time k-colouring conjecture for graphs with maximal local edge-connectivity k
record.statement:
Let $k\geq 4$ be fixed, and let $G$ be a graph with **maximal local edge-connectivity** $k$, meaning that the maximum local edge-connectivity over all pairs of vertices of $G$ is $k$. A $k$-colouring of $G$ is a proper vertex colouring using at most $k$ colours.

**Polynomial-time k-colouring conjecture.** There is a polynomial-time algorithm that, given $G$, finds a $k$-colouring of $G$, or determines that none exists.

The conjecture concerns the unresolved complexity of $k$-colouring for graphs with maximal local edge-connectivity $k$ when $k\geq 4$, following polynomial-time results for narrower connectivity classes and NP-completeness results for related colouring problems.
record.source_name: Pierre Aboulker, Nick Brettell, Frédéric Havet, Dániel Marx and Nicolas Trotignon, “Colouring graphs with constraints on connectivity”, arXiv:1505.01616 (2016).

record.title: De Pierro's conjecture on underrelaxed projection limits
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a real Hilbert space and let $C_1,\ldots,C_N$ be nonempty closed convex subsets of $X$, with metric projections $P_{C_i}$. For $\lambda\in]0,1]$, define

$$
Q_{\lambda}:=((1-\lambda)Id+\lambda P_{C_N})\cdots((1-\lambda)Id+\lambda P_{C_2})((1-\lambda)Id+\lambda P_{C_1}).
$$

Assume that $F_{\lambda}:=\operatorname*{Fix}Q_{\lambda}\neq\emptyset$ for every $\lambda\in]0,1]$. For $x\in X$, let

$$
x_{\lambda}=\operatorname*{weak}\lim_{n\rightarrow+\infty}Q_{\lambda}^{n}(x).
$$

Let $\mathcal{L}$ be the set of least-squares solutions,

$$
\mathcal{L}:=\left\{x\in X\mid \sum_{i=1}^{N}\left\Vert x-P_{C_i}(x)\right\Vert^2=\inf_{y\in X}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\left\Vert y-P_{C_i}(y)\right\Vert^2\right\}.
$$

**De Pierro's conjecture.** The weak limits satisfy

$$
\lim_{\lambda\rightarrow0^{+}}x_{\lambda}=P_{\mathcal{L}}(x).
$$

The conjecture concerns the behavior, as the underrelaxation parameter tends to zero, of weak limits generated by cyclic compositions of underrelaxed projections for inconsistent convex feasibility problems. It is false in general: a system of three compact convex sets in $\mathbb{R}^{3}$ provides a counterexample.
record.source_name: Yair Censor and Maroun Zaknoon, “Algorithms and Convergence Results of Projection Methods for Inconsistent Feasibility Problems: A Review”, arXiv:1802.07529 (2018).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2018). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1801.03216](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.03216).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.07529

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of February 2018).

record.title: The generalized vector space partition conjecture for $A_q(2k,2k-2;k)$
record.statement:
Let $A_q(n,d;k)$ denote the maximum size of a constant-dimension $k$-subspace code in $\mathbb{F}_q^n$ with minimum subspace distance at least $d$. **Generalized vector space partition conjecture.** For each $k\ge 4$,

$$
A_q(2k,2k-2;k)=q^{2k}+1.
$$

This conjecture concerns the extremal size of constant-dimension codes with parameters $(2k,2k-2;k)$ and is motivated by the known bound in the case $A_2(8,6;4)$. The source gives only tiny numerical evidence and presents the claim as a conjecture, so its general validity remains open.
record.source_name: Daniel Heinlein, Thomas Honold, Michael Kiermaier and Sascha Kurz, “Generalized vector space partitions”, arXiv:1803.10180 (2019).

record.title: Cheeger constant conjecture for distance-regular graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a distance-regular graph, let $h_G$ denote its Cheeger constant, and let $\lambda_1$ be the smallest positive eigenvalue of the Laplacian matrix of $G$.

**Cheeger constant conjecture.**

$$
\frac{\lambda_1}{2} \leq h_G \leq \lambda_1.
$$

The lower bound is the general Cheeger inequality, while the conjectured upper bound improves the general spectral upper bound for distance-regular graphs. The conjecture is supported by results for known infinite families, diameter-two graphs, several classes of diameter-three graphs, and most distance-regular graphs with small valency.
record.source_name: Jack Koolen, Greg Markowsky and Zhi Qiao, “On the Cheeger constant for distance-regular graphs”, arXiv:1811.00230 (2019).

record.title: The edge domination conjecture for connected regular graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite, simple, connected, $\Delta$-regular graph of order $n$, where $\Delta\geq 3$. The **edge domination conjecture** asserts that

$$
\gamma_e(G)\leq \frac{2\Delta-1}{4\Delta}n+\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Equality holds if and only if $G$ has a spanning subgraph that is the union of an odd number of copies of $K_{\Delta,\Delta}-e$. This conjecture would give a best-possible upper bound on the minimum size of a maximal matching in connected regular graphs, with an explicit characterization of the equality cases.
record.source_name: Julien Baste, Maximilian Fürst, Michael A. Henning, Elena Mohr and Dieter Rautenbach, “Bounding and approximating minimum maximal matchings in regular graphs”, arXiv:1905.12241 (2019).

record.title: The 1–2–3 Conjecture for neighbour-sum-distinguishing edge weightings
record.statement: Let $G$ be a connected graph with at least three vertices. An edge weighting assigns a weight from $\{1,2,3\}$ to every edge of $G$, and the sum at a vertex is the sum of the weights on its incident edges. **1–2–3 Conjecture.** Every such graph has an edge weighting for which adjacent vertices receive distinct sums of their incident weights. This conjecture asks whether three edge weights always suffice to distinguish the incident-weight sums of adjacent vertices; it remains open in general, although the paper proves the Standard $(2,2)$-Conjecture for graphs with sufficiently large minimum degree.
record.source_name: Jakub Przybyło, “On the Standard (2,2)-Conjecture”, arXiv:1911.00867 (2019).

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2019).

record.title: The extremal characterization of global amoeba graphs of minimum degree one
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a global amoeba graph of order $n$ and minimum degree $1$. Let $e(G)$ denote its number of edges, let $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor$ be the floor of $n^2/4$, and let $H_n$ be the graph defined in Example 2(c) of the source.

**Extremal global amoeba conjecture.**

$$
e(G)=\left\lfloor\frac{n^2}{4}\right\rfloor
$$

if and only if $G\cong H_n$.

The graph $H_n$ is shown to have the largest density among global amoebas of minimum degree $1$; the conjecture asserts that it is the unique graph attaining this extremal edge count, up to isomorphism.

record.title: Conjecture on nonvanishing determinant conditions for lattice codes
record.statement:
Let $n\geq m$, let $\mathcal{L}$ be a $2mn$-dimensional lattice in $M_n(\mathbb{C})$, and suppose that

$$
\Delta_m(\mathcal{L})\neq 0.
$$

Here $\Delta_m(\mathcal{L})$ denotes the infimum of the products of the smallest $m$ singular values of nonzero elements of $\mathcal{L}$. **Nonvanishing determinant condition conjecture.** The conditions of Corollary can be satisfied only when either $m=n$ or when $n=2$ and $m=1$. This concerns when a $2mn$-dimensional lattice code in $M_n(\mathbb{C})$ can satisfy the nonvanishing product-of-singular-values condition required for approximate universality with $m$ receive antennas. The claim is presented as conjectural, and no resolution is given in the source.
record.source_name: Roope Vehkalahti and Laura Luzzi, “The DMT of Real and Quaternionic Lattice Codes and DMT Classification of Division Algebra Codes”, arXiv:2102.09910 (2021).

record.title: The decomposition conjecture for class II graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with maximum degree $\Delta$ and edge-chromatic number $\chi'(G)=\Delta+k$, and let $p,q$ be positive integers satisfying

$$
p+q=\Delta+k
$$

with $p,q\leq\Delta$. A graph is **class I** if its edge-chromatic number equals its maximum degree. **Decomposition conjecture.** The graph $G$ can be decomposed into two class I subgraphs $H_1$ and $H_2$ such that

$$
\Delta(H_1)=p,\qquad \Delta(H_2)=q.
$$

This would generalize the preceding theorem, which gives a decomposition with maximum degrees $\Delta$ and $k$; the proposed statement allows any two positive maximum degrees at most $\Delta$ whose sum is $\Delta+k$.
record.source_name: Yan Cao, Guangming Jing, Rong Luo, Vahan Mkrtchyan, Cun-Quan Zhang and Yue Zhao, “Decomposition of class II graphs into two class I graphs”, arXiv:2211.05930 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.05930

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2022).

record.title: The maximum matching conjecture for maximum edge-colorable subgraphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an $r$-regular graph with maximum degree $\Delta$ and edge-chromatic number $\chi'(G)=\Delta+1$. A **maximum $\Delta$-colorable subgraph** is a subgraph with as many edges as possible whose edge-chromatic number is at most $\Delta$, and let $M$ be a maximum matching of $G$. **Maximum matching conjecture.** There is a maximum $\Delta$-colorable subgraph $H$ of $G$ such that

$$
M\cup E(H)=E(G).
$$

This is proposed as a generalization of a theorem of Mkrtchyan and Steffen for bridgeless cubic graphs and perfect matchings. The conjecture asks whether the matching-completion property persists for regular class II graphs.
